title: Concepts of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a system by which class, status, and power are organized in a hierarchy. Societies allocate resources unequally, leading to distinct layers with varying levels of privilege and opportunity.

Multiple theoretical frameworks attempt to explain the persistence of these divisions. Functionalism suggests that inequality is necessary for societal efficiency, as differing rewards motivate people to fill essential roles. Conversely, conflict theory views stratification primarily as a mechanism through which dominant groups maintain power and exploit subordinate classes.
